Cloud/SSH/npm credential file access by Node or Bun during npm install AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the credential harvesting stage of Mini Shai-Hulud: Node or Bun (when spawned within an npm install context) reading developer secret stores — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_*, gh hosts.yml, kubeconfig, .docker/config.json, Vault tokens. These files are read by the malware to enumerate cloud/CI credentials before exfil. Rationale: Wiz, Snyk, Socket and Unit42 all enumerate the same harvest target set (AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/GitHub/npm/SSH/Vault). Detecting node or bun in install-context fanning out across ≥3 of these distinct cred file types within a single process group is the highest-signal behavioural pivot the malware leaves before exfiltrating to t.m-kosche.com. Anti-pattern-aware: threshold and process gate suppress benign single-file reads (npm reads ~/.npmrc every install on its own). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS CDK / Pulumi / Serverless framework legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials during deploy
  • GitHub CLI extension or git-credential-manager being invoked from a node-based pre-commit hook
  • Developer running `npm run deploy` that touches kube + docker + aws creds in sequence
  • Test harness that reads .npmrc, kubeconfig and .docker/config.json to validate dev environment setup
  • Node-based dotfile manager / chezmoi-style tool legitimately enumerating dotfiles
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-cdk","@aws-cdk","pulumi","serverless","@serverless","sst","chezmoi","git-credential-manager") and PathsTouched !has_any ("setup.mjs","execution.js"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full set of paths touched within the InitiatingProcessId window — true positives almost always span >3 distinct cred ecosystems (AWS+SSH+npm+GitHub), legitimate tools usually touch one. Correlate the host against UC1 (t.m-kosche.com egress) and UC2 (bun spawned by npm) — any two of three confirms incident. Step 2 — Contain: revoke EVERY credential matching the touched files (rotate AWS keys, regenerate SSH keypairs, revoke GitHub PAT + npm token, regenerate kubeconfigs). Isolate host, snapshot, do not wipe — preserve evidence of what was harvested. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate the developer's recent npm installs (npm-debug.log, ~/.npm/_logs) to identify the entry-point package; cross-reference to the Mini Shai-Hulud package list and notify any downstream consumers if the developer published packages of their own in the last 14 days.
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest: node/bun touching multiple secret stores during install
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.ssh\known_hosts", @"/.ssh/known_hosts",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\gcloud\credentials.db", @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"\.azure\msal_token_cache", @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpenInfo","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js","npm ci","npm i ")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (credPaths) or FileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(FolderPath, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
  by DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest via ASIM file events
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (credPaths) or TargetFileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:11 AND @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) AND @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials* OR *\.aws\config* OR *\.npmrc* OR *\.ssh\id_* OR *\.config\gh\hosts.yml* OR *\.kube\config* OR *\.docker\config.json* OR *.vault-token* OR *\.azure\msal_token_cache*)) OR (source:linux.auditd AND @process.name:(node OR bun OR npm OR yarn OR pnpm) AND @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config* OR */.npmrc* OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml* OR */.kube/config* OR */.docker/config.json* OR */.vault-token* OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db* OR */.azure/msal_token_cache*))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) ContextImageFileName=/(node|bun|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$/i | TargetFileName=/(\\\.aws\\(credentials|config)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\\\.npmrc|\/\.npmrc|\\\.ssh\\id_|\/\.ssh\/id_|\\\.config\\gh\\hosts\.yml|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\\\.kube\\config|\/\.kube\/config|\\\.docker\\config\.json|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\.vault-token|\/\.config\/gcloud\/credentials\.db|\/\.azure\/msal_token_cache)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths), collect(TargetFileName)]) | DistinctPaths >= 3 | sort(DistinctPaths, order=desc)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*.vault-token*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*GITHUB_TOKEN*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*NPM_TOKEN*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(paths) >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AVideo YPTSocket plugin XSS injection via webSocketSelfURI/page_title query strings AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated exploitation of GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 in WWBN AVideo by detecting HTTP requests to the YPTSocket token endpoint or WebSocket upgrade carrying HTML/JS payloads in the webSocketSelfURI or page_title query parameters. The payload is then broadcast to any admin viewing a page that renders the YPTSocket debug panel. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint path /plugin/YPTSocket/ and the two attacker-controlled parameters (webSocketSelfURI, page_title) named in functions.php:21-24 and MessageSQLiteV2.php:91/110, combined with URL-encoded and raw HTML/JS payload tokens (including the article's String.fromCharCode evasion). Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory text and the AVideo repo paths cited in the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 • https://github.com/WWBN/AVideo
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal QA/security teams pentesting the YPTSocket plugin (legitimate XSS test payloads)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Burp Suite, Nuclei, ZAP) probing AVideo with HTML/JS canary payloads
  • Bug-bounty researchers replaying the PoC against staging
  • Legitimate AVideo dashboards passing rich page titles that happen to contain '<' (rare — utf8_encode source values normally don't carry HTML)
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("Burp", "Nuclei", "ZAP", "sqlmap", "nikto") and SrcIp !in ("<internal_pentest_ranges>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull all hits on /plugin/YPTSocket/getWebSocket.json.php and the WebSocket upgrade with these parameters in the last 48h; URL-decode the query string and identify the actual JS payload, source IP, and User-Agent. Confirm whether the AVideo instance has the YPTSocket plugin enabled and debugSocket=true (the vulnerable default). Step 2 — Contain: block the offending source IP at the WAF/edge, disable the YPTSocket plugin or set debugSocket=false until patched (upgrade composer:WWBN/AVideo above 29.0), and force-rotate admin session cookies and CSRF tokens for any admin who was logged in during the window. Step 3 — Hunt: review admin-context API calls (user/role mutations, password changes, plugin enable/disable, content edits) from admin session IDs that overlap with the broadcast window; pivot on AdminUser browser sessions to outbound exfil to attacker-controlled domains in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("webSocketSelfURI=", "page_title=")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("%3Cimg", "%3Cscript", "onerror%3D", "onload%3D", "%3Csvg", "javascript%3A", "String.fromCharCode", "%3Ciframe", "<img", "<script", "onerror=", "onload=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectTokens = dynamic(["%3Cimg","%3Cscript","onerror%3D","onload%3D","%3Csvg","javascript%3A","String.fromCharCode","%3Ciframe","<img","<script","onerror=","onload=","fromCharCode"]);

    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs

Talos weekly prevalent malware SHA256 IOC sweep (Coinminer / Procpatcher / KMS activator) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts process executions and file writes matching the five SHA256 hashes Talos called out as the week's most prevalent malware in their 2026-06-04 newsletter telemetry roundup. Covers Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (sample.exe), W32.C0AD494457-95 (f_000b97.html), and PUA.Win.Tool.Kmsactivator (AutoPico.exe). Rationale: Detection is grounded on the five SHA256 hashes Talos explicitly named in the 'Most prevalent malware files' block (VID001.exe Coinminer, sample.exe Procpatcher, f_000b97.html W32.C0AD494457-95, AutoPico.exe Kmsactivator, plus the fifth truncated entry). These are confirmed-bad per Talos detection names — file-reputation match is the highest-fidelity signal possible from this article. No external sources cross-checked: the IOC list is a weekly Talos telemetry snapshot from today's date with no second source yet published.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analysts intentionally detonating samples in a sandbox / malware-analysis VM (especially analysts retrieving Talos-flagged hashes for testing)
  • AutoPico.exe / KMS activator hash firing on unlicensed Windows installs (common in test/lab environments and unmanaged dev boxes)
  • f_000b97.html cached in browser cache directories from a benign visit — file write triggers without execution (review FolderPath for browser cache paths before escalating)
  • EDR vendor sample-collection / threat intel platforms (CrowdStrike, MDE attack surface reduction telemetry) pulling sample copies for analysis
  • Legitimate AV scanners writing the sample to quarantine — initiating process being the AV engine itself
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !contains "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !contains "\\Sandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","CSFalconService.exe","SenseIR.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the matching event's FolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, and AccountName. If folder is a known sandbox/quarantine path (e.g. C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine, sandbox VM paths) or parent is an AV engine, downgrade. Confirm the Talos detection name from the case statement against the article's labelling. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR network containment. Kill the live process tree; quarantine the file. For Coinminer (VID001.exe) check for persistence via Run keys and scheduled tasks; for Procpatcher review which process was patched (often AV/EDR tampering). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName to find the delivery vector (browser download? email attachment? USB?). Sweep the rest of the fleet for the same SHA256 over 30 days and for the parent's hash. If KMS activator triggered, audit the host for other PUA / cracked software via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory.

let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (TalosMalwareHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Source = "DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents

union ProcHits, FileHits

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

            - '\pwsh.exe'

            - 'invoke-expression'

            - 'hxxp'

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path · [LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path AICommand & Control High
Hunts the specific KongTuke (TAG-124 / 404 TDS) command-and-control infrastructure named in the Talos case study: outbound HTTP to 144.31.221.82 on TCP/6060 with a URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint. Single-IOC alerting because all three values are article-named. Rationale: Single high-confidence IOC bundle straight from the Talos case-study paragraph: IP 144.31.221.82, TCP/6060, URL path /capcha9856. The /capcha* fingerprint is corroborated by Recorded Future (TAG-124), Red Canary KongTuke profile, and malware-traffic-analysis.net Jan 2026 KongTuke ClickFix capture. Cross-checked via WebSearch — KongTuke is a real, active TDS. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base • https://www.malware-traffic-analysis.net/2026/01/08/index.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal pentest or red-team rehearsal targeting the same IOC after reading the Talos blog
  • Threat-intel platform or DFIR sandbox automatically dialling out to known-bad C2 for verification (e.g. JoeSandbox, ANY.RUN agent on a corp jump host)
  • Threat-hunt tooling that replays packet captures with the destination IP rewritten for test purposes
  • Security awareness training simulator using captured KongTuke traffic
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("smss.exe","wininit.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","sbox","detonation","malsandbox"))
Response runbook
Triage: Confirm the source host is a real production endpoint, then pull DeviceProcessEvents on it for ±30 min around the connection. Look for cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → curl.exe chain that Talos documented. Check Defender/AMP for any blocked-detection signatures on the same host. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender for Endpoint / Falcon Network Containment. Block 144.31.221.82 + the /capcha URL pattern at the firewall and proxy. Force-reset the logged-in user's credentials. Hunt: Sweep the entire estate for any other endpoint connecting to 144.31.221.82, port 6060, or any URL containing /capcha. Check WordPress/CMS site referrer logs for which compromised site redirected the user (TDS chains). Submit the IP to TI vendors and enrol the URL-path pattern into the proxy as a hunt rule.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
   or RemoteUrl has "/capcha9856"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessParentFileName, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DeviceVendor =~ "Cisco" or DeviceProduct has "Firepower" or DeviceProduct has "Secure Firewall" or isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82"
   or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
   or RequestURL has "/capcha9856"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort,
          RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceAction, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: KongTuke TDS C2 to 144.31.221.82 / capcha URL Path
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a01
description: Detects outbound network traffic to KongTuke TDS C2 infrastructure (144.31.221.82:6060) or any URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint reported by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
  - https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '144.31.221.82'
  selection_port_path:
    DestinationPort: 6060
    DestinationHostname|contains: '/capcha'
  selection_path:
    Url|contains: '/capcha9856'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_port_path or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - None expected; this IP/port/path combination has no known legitimate use.
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:cisco-firepower OR source:cisco_secure_firewall) AND (@DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 OR (@DestinationPort:6060 AND @DestinationHostname:*\/capcha*) OR @network.destination.ip:144.31.221.82 OR @url:*\/capcha9856*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82" OR RemotePort=6060)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/capcha/i}, field=aid, include=[DomainName], mode=left)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.url) as urls values(All_Traffic.app) as apps from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="144.31.221.82" AND All_Traffic.dest_port=6060) OR (All_Traffic.url="*/capcha9856*" OR All_Traffic.url="*/capcha*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.url) as urls values(All_Traffic.app) as apps from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest="144.31.221.82" AND All_Traffic.dest_port=6060) OR (All_Traffic.url="*/capcha9856*" OR All_Traffic.url="*/capcha*") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the KongTuke stage-2 download pattern from the Talos case study: a powershell.exe process whose command line invokes Invoke-WebRequest (or iwr) and writes a file named script.ps1 into the user's ApplicationData / AppData directory. Pairs the URL-fetch verb, the article-named filename, and the article-named drop location in one event. Rationale: The combination of three article-named tokens in one PowerShell command line — Invoke-WebRequest verb, exact filename script.ps1, and AppData/ApplicationData drop path — collapses to one cmdline-substring detection that's high specificity. Sourced directly from the Talos KongTuke walk-through (cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → IWR → script.ps1 → ApplicationData). Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1105 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin debugging an internal PowerShell module by manually fetching a generic 'script.ps1' into AppData
  • Software install wrapper that downloads a setup script (rename script.ps1 → install.ps1 is more common, but some installers do this)
  • Red-team / atomic-red-team test cases that mirror the KongTuke download chain
  • Security researcher rehydrating IOCs in a lab VM joined to corporate Defender
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("vscode.exe","code.exe","devenv.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe") and not (DeviceName has_any ("sbx","sandbox","redteam","atomic"))
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the parent process tree for the powershell.exe event — confirm parent is cmd.exe spawned from a browser process (chrome/edge/firefox), which matches the TDS-redirect chain. Decode any preceding -EncodedCommand on the same PID. Hash and submit the dropped script.ps1 (still in %AppData%) to sandbox; capture content before Remove-Item runs. Contain: Isolate the host. Suspend the affected user account. Block C2 144.31.221.82 + /capcha pattern at egress. Hunt: Sweep estate for any powershell.exe with script.ps1 + AppData in cmdline. Pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents for that PID/host and confirm C2 callback. Pull browser history for the user to find the compromised WordPress redirector that launched the TDS chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr ", "Net.WebClient", "DownloadFile", "DownloadString")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "script.ps1"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("AppData", "ApplicationData", "\\Roaming\\", "\\Local\\")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest", "iwr ", "Net.WebClient", "DownloadFile", "DownloadString")
| where CommandLine has "script.ps1"
| where CommandLine has_any ("AppData", "ApplicationData", "\\Roaming\\", "\\Local\\")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: KongTuke PowerShell Drops script.ps1 to AppData via Invoke-WebRequest
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a02
description: Detects PowerShell command line that fetches a remote file named script.ps1 and writes it into the user's AppData directory — the KongTuke stage-2 download chain documented by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_fetch:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'DownloadString'
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains: 'script.ps1'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'AppData'
      - 'ApplicationData'
      - '\Roaming\'
      - '\Local\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal scripts that happen to fetch a file named script.ps1 into AppData (rare; review user context)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (@CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *iwr\ * OR *Net.WebClient* OR *DownloadFile* OR *DownloadString*)) AND @CommandLine:*script.ps1* AND (@CommandLine:(*AppData* OR *ApplicationData* OR *\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Local\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|iwr |Net\.WebClient|DownloadFile|DownloadString)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("script\.ps1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(AppData|ApplicationData|\\\\Roaming\\\\|\\\\Local\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window AICommand & Control High
Reproduces the Talos multi-source-correlation insight: the same endpoint reaching 144.31.221.82 from two distinct binaries (powershell.exe via Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe directly) is the disambiguating signal that turned a single firewall hit into a confirmed intrusion. Single-binary callouts to the IP are already caught by UC1; this UC fires on the host-level fan-out only. Rationale: Directly encodes the Talos case-study insight: 'a separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Two distinct LOLBin/native binaries calling the same KongTuke IP from one host is high-fidelity even without the URL-path filter — it's the multi-process fan-out that confirms intrusion vs single-shot scanning. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT troubleshooting a connectivity issue, running both Test-NetConnection (PowerShell) and curl against the same external host
  • Monitoring agents (e.g. uptime checks) that issue parallel HTTP probes from multiple wrappers
  • Red-team simulation reproducing the Talos case study against the same IOCs
  • Custom CMDB sync script that uses both powershell IWR and curl for redundancy
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("ops-","jumpbox-","netops-")) and not (AccountName has_any ("netops","sre","itadmin"))
Response runbook
Triage: Pull the process trees for both the powershell.exe and curl.exe events — confirm common parent or temporal proximity (<10 min). Decode any -EncodedCommand on the powershell side; capture curl.exe full command-line (URL, headers, output path). Verify the destination IP/path against KongTuke IOC list. Contain: Isolate the host. Force a credential reset for the logged-in user. Block 144.31.221.82 + /capcha pattern at proxy and firewall. Snapshot the host for memory analysis before reimage. Hunt: Run UC1 + UC2 across the estate to find any other host hitting KongTuke. Pivot on the IP via VirusTotal / Shodan for sibling infrastructure; add ASN to network-egress hunt block. Check email gateway for any KongTuke-themed lure URL that arrived in the 24h before first observation.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82" or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe")
| summarize ProcessSet = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            FirstConnection = min(Timestamp),
            LastConnection = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            CmdLines = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 8)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(ProcessSet) >= 2
| where (ProcessSet has "curl.exe") and (ProcessSet has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| order by FirstConnection desc
let WindowHours = 1h;
let FirewallHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82" or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
    | project FirewallTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL;
let ProcessHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("144.31.221.82", "capcha", "script.ps1")
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | project ProcessTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName;
FirewallHits
| join kind=inner (
    ProcessHits
    | summarize Procs=make_set(NewProcessName), AnyCmd=make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer
    | where array_length(Procs) >= 2
) on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| order by FirewallTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\Curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82"
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[collect([ContextImageFileName]), count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
| length(ContextImageFileName) >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Processes.process_name) as distinct_procs values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe") (Processes.process="*144.31.221.82*" OR Processes.process="*capcha*") by Processes.dest Processes.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where distinct_procs >= 2
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Processes.process_name) as distinct_procs values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmdlines min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe") (Processes.process="*144.31.221.82*" OR Processes.process="*capcha*") by Processes.dest Processes.user host
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where distinct_procs >= 2
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("144.31.221.82") or RemoteUrl has_any ("")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["144.31.221.82"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic([""]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("144.31.221.82")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("")

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_* YAML-injection payload AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP POSTs to the Jupyter Enterprise Gateway `/api/kernels` endpoint whose body carries `KERNEL_WORKING_DIR`, `KERNEL_POD_NAME`, `KERNEL_NAMESPACE` or other `KERNEL_*` env values containing YAML-injection markers (`---`, `...`, embedded `securityContext`, `runAsUser`, `privileged`). This is the exact CVE-2026-44182 exploit shape — the unsanitised env-var is interpolated into the Jinja2 pod manifest at kernel-pod.yaml.j2 line 77 and lets the caller overwrite or append Kubernetes resources. Rationale: Anchors on the exact exploit primitive from the GHSA PoC: a POST to /api/kernels carrying KERNEL_WORKING_DIR/KERNEL_POD_NAME/KERNEL_NAMESPACE whose value embeds a YAML breakout (`\n# INJECTION\n securityContext:\n runAsUser: 0` or `...\n---\napiVersion: v1\nkind: Pod`). The Jinja2 line referenced (kernel-pod.yaml.j2#L77) and the launch_kubernetes.py uppercase→lowercase conversion (lines 130-137) confirm these are the only attacker-controlled fields. No second-source corroboration searched — single advisory CVE. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfw7-6c5v-2wjq
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1611
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate JupyterHub spawner submits KERNEL_WORKING_DIR with `--profile` or `--name` containing literal dashes that match `---`
  • QA / penetration-test environments where security teams replay the PoC against staging EG
  • EG client SDKs that base64-encode env values; markers won't match but raw KERNEL_ entries still log
  • Kernel-launchers that legitimately pass multi-line YAML (kernel resources, tolerations) through `KERNEL_EXTRA_SPEC_MUTATIONS`
  • Verbose debug logging that echoes the rendered manifest back to syslog, double-matching on the same event
Suppression filter
| where not(Evidence has_any ("--profile", "--kernel-name", "--spec-name")) | where not(ProcessName has "debug" and Evidence has "rendered manifest")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the matching POST body and confirm a `KERNEL_*` value contains a literal `\n` or `---`/`...` followed by `securityContext`/`runAsUser`/`privileged`. Identify the source IP and whether it sits inside the JupyterHub auth boundary. 2) Contain: scale enterprise-gateway to 0 or block the source IP at ingress; revoke any kernel pods spawned by the affected EG instance in the kernel namespace (e.g. `notebooks`) within the alert window; rotate the EG ServiceAccount token. 3) Hunt: query AKSAudit/EKS audit for pods created by the EG ServiceAccount with `privileged:true`, `runAsUser:0`, `hostPath` mounts, or `hostNetwork:true` over the past 30 days; check whether `mirrorWorkingDirs` / `EG_MIRROR_WORKING_DIRS` is set; review egress from any spawned kernel container for reverse-shell traffic.
// Endpoint-tier visibility only — looks for outbound connections from a host to the EG service
// where the EG ingress is reachable internally; pair with WAF/ingress body inspection in Sentinel.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (31529, 8888, 8889, 8443)
| where RemoteUrl has "/api/kernels" or AdditionalFields has "/api/kernels"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Detects KERNEL_* env-var with YAML-injection markers in EG application syslog or WAF body logs.
// CommonSecurityLog does NOT carry DeviceName — use DestinationHostName / SourceIP for host pivots.
let InjectionMarkers = @"(?i)KERNEL_[A-Z_]+[^\n]{0,200}(---|\.\.\.|securityContext|runAsUser|runAsGroup|fsGroup|privileged\s*:\s*true)";
union isfuzzy=true
(
  Syslog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessName has_any ("enterprise_gateway", "enterprise-gateway", "jupyter") or SyslogMessage has "/api/kernels"
  | where SyslogMessage matches regex InjectionMarkers
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="Syslog", Host=Computer, HostName, ProcessName, Evidence=SyslogMessage
),
(
  CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where RequestURL has "/api/kernels" and RequestMethod =~ "POST"
  | where Message matches regex InjectionMarkers or DeviceCustomString1 matches regex InjectionMarkers or AdditionalExtensions matches regex InjectionMarkers
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="WAF/Proxy", Host=DestinationHostName, SourceIP=SourceIP, ProcessName=DeviceProduct, Evidence=coalesce(Message, DeviceCustomString1, AdditionalExtensions)
),
(
  W3CIISLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where csUriStem == "/api/kernels" and csMethod =~ "POST"
  | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Host=Computer, SourceIP=cIP, ProcessName="w3wp", Evidence=strcat(csMethod, " ", csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Privileged or root pod created by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount AIInstallation High
Detects the Kubernetes-API-server-side effect of CVE-2026-44182: a Pod created by the enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount whose spec contains `privileged: true`, `runAsUser: 0`, `runAsGroup: 0`, a `hostPath` mount, or `hostNetwork: true`. EG should only ever spawn unprivileged kernel pods running as uid 1000 (jovyan); any privileged spec from this SA is the post-injection footprint. Rationale: Anchors on the EG-default identity (the `enterprise-gateway` ServiceAccount, see Helm chart) and the article-stated effects: the PoC explicitly produces pods with `privileged:true, runAsUser:0, runAsGroup:0` and notes the impact extends to arbitrary `hostPath` mounts. Normal EG kernel pods run as `uid=1000(jovyan)` per the rendered template — any privileged/root spec from this SA is the injection footprint, not noise. Only the original GHSA cross-checked. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cfw7-6c5v-2wjq • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/kernel-pod.yaml.j2#L77 • https://github.com/jupyter-server/enterprise_gateway/blob/152c20f162f2fab700c04c8830ebf8c1e2e2217a/etc/kernel-launchers/kubernetes/scripts/launch_kubernetes.py#L130-L137
ATT&CKT1611 T1068 T1190
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator-driven EG redeploy that legitimately needs `hostPath` for a custom kernel image (should appear in change tickets)
  • Cluster admins testing EG with a non-default kernel launcher that sets `runAsUser: 0` intentionally for a GPU-pinned kernel
  • Kustomize/Helm upgrade where EG SA temporarily reapplies a kernel-pod template that includes a deprecated `securityContext` block
  • Pod Security Admission webhook re-emits the requestObject during validation, double-logging the same create
  • Internal scanner (kube-bench, Falco rule replay) replaying a known privileged-pod manifest against EG SA in a test namespace
Suppression filter
| where Caller !has "system:serviceaccount:kube-system" | where not(RequestObject has "gpu" and RequestObject has "nvidia.com/gpu") | where Namespace !in ("eg-staging", "eg-test", "sandbox-notebooks")
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the matched AKSAudit/CloudTrail record, extract `objectRef.name` and `objectRef.namespace`, and confirm the requestObject contains a privileged field that was not in any pinned EG template (compare against the Helm-rendered baseline). Capture the source IP from `sourceIPs[]`. 2) Contain: delete the offending pod (`kubectl delete pod -n <ns> <name>`), cordon the node it landed on, scale `enterprise-gateway` to 0, and rotate the EG ServiceAccount token + kernel-namespace ServiceAccount tokens. If `hostPath` was mounted, treat the node as compromised and reimage. 3) Hunt: enumerate every pod the EG SA has created in the last 30 days where `runAsUser==0` or `privileged==true` or any `hostPath`; pull egress flow logs from those pod IPs for C2 indicators; check the EG ingress access logs for `/api/kernels` POSTs with `KERNEL_*` injection markers and pivot back to UC1.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb == "create"
| where tostring(ObjectRef) has "\"resource\":\"pods\""
| where Stage == "ResponseComplete"
| where tostring(User) has_any ("enterprise-gateway", "enterprise_gateway")
| where tostring(RequestObject) has_any ("\"privileged\":true", "\"runAsUser\":0", "\"runAsGroup\":0", "\"hostNetwork\":true", "\"hostPID\":true", "hostPath")
| extend PodName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).name)
| extend Namespace = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).namespace)
| extend Caller = tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Caller, Namespace, PodName, Verb, RequestUri, RequestObject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels (CVE-2026-44181)
